briefs.headline: Alonso says James' knee layoff 'won't be short'
briefs.summary: Chelsea's manager said Friday the club gives no timelines but the captain's absence will run "a few weeks" and perhaps past Christmas; James has not played since Sept. 12. Chelsea visit Everton at 7:30 a.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Hannan routs St. Marys 11-2 to finish the regular season 5-5-1
briefs.summary: Hannan led 9-0 at halftime Thursday at Ashton, per the MaxPreps box score posted Friday; the keeper made six saves. The result arrived a day after the match showed no score.

briefs.headline: Hannan draws No. 7 seed, opens regional play against Tug Valley
briefs.summary: The WVSSAC Class AA-A Region IV bracket, posted Friday, sends No. 10 Tug Valley to Hannan in the first round with No. 2 Buffalo waiting Oct. 21; regional champions reach the state tournament in Beckley Nov. 4 to 7.

briefs.headline: Concepcion cleared to play as Ravens rule out Jackson
briefs.summary: The rookie receiver, who leads Cleveland with 29 targets, cleared concussion protocol Friday; Baltimore said Lamar Jackson misses a second game with his ankle and Tyler Huntley starts Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

briefs.headline: Spurs beat Kings 126-97, will start three guards in opener
briefs.summary: Dylan Harper scored 19 in Friday's final preseason game in San Antonio, and coach Mitch Johnson said the Fox-Castle-Harper lineup starts Tuesday's 9:30 p.m. ET opener against Oklahoma City on NBC.

briefs.headline: Rain pushes ALCS Game 4 to Saturday and Game 5 to Sunday
briefs.summary: Friday's game in Cleveland was called late in the evening; it is 8 p.m. ET tonight on TBS with Nick Martinez starting for Tampa Bay and Shawn Armstrong opening for Cleveland, which leads two games to one. Game 5 is 5 p.m. ET Sunday.

briefs.headline: Dombrowski tells Turner to fix his defense or change positions
briefs.summary: The Phillies executive said Thursday the shortstop, who made a league-worst 21 errors and hit .242, must show by spring training he can play the position; seven years remain on his $300 million contract.

briefs.headline: Eagles rule out Barkley; McKee starts for Hurts against Panthers
briefs.summary: Saquon Barkley's hamstring keeps him out Sunday, and Jalen Hurts sits with a superficial blood clot in his calf that the team said a Wednesday ultrasound showed had moved; DeVonta Smith is set to return after two games.

briefs.headline: Titans CEO backs Saleh and Borgonzi through winless start of five games
briefs.summary: Burke Nihill told ESPN on Friday the organization believes in its coach and general manager and will be patient; Tennessee's offense averages a league-low 246.4 yards and 11.6 points, and the defense has two takeaways.

briefs.headline: MacKinnon has four points as Avalanche rally past Penguins 5-2
briefs.summary: Evgeni Malkin and Bryan Rust scored 29 seconds apart for a two-goal Pittsburgh lead Friday in Denver before Colorado answered with five straight, two by Artturi Lehkonen; Sidney Crosby's 1,110th assist moved him to seventh all-time.

briefs.headline: Lindholm's third period carries Bruins past Ducks 4-2
briefs.summary: Elias Lindholm set up the tying goal and scored the go-ahead goal Friday in Anaheim as Boston erased an early two-goal deficit for a fourth straight win; David Pastrnak's 423rd goal passed Brad Marchand for fourth in Bruins history.

briefs.headline: Tkachuk scores second straight natural hat trick as Panthers beat Canucks 3-2
briefs.summary: Brady Tkachuk's overtime winner Thursday in Sunrise made him the third player in NHL history, and the first since 1986, with three consecutive goals in back-to-back games; Florida came from behind to win.

briefs.headline: CFP reaches 'handshake agreement' with ESPN on 24-team playoff
briefs.summary: Sources told ESPN on Friday the network would pay an average $345 million a year more over five years, on top of $1.3 billion, for a format starting in 2027 that ends Power 4 title games; boards on all sides must still approve.

briefs.headline: Washington ends three-game skid with 38-26 win at Purdue
briefs.summary: Elijah Brown threw for 302 yards and three touchdowns Friday in his first Huskies start, overcoming three interceptions; Trey Cooley's 53-yard run sealed it, and Washington is 4-3.

briefs.headline: Tulane forces six turnovers in 31-17 win over Memphis
briefs.summary: TJ Smith returned an interception 76 yards on the final play of the first half Friday in New Orleans; Memphis quarterback Marcus Stokes threw four interceptions and lost two fumbles as the Tigers fell to 5-2.

briefs.headline: Hall of Famer Cliff Hagan dies at 94
briefs.summary: Kentucky, where he won the 1951 NCAA title and later served as athletic director, announced his death Friday; the five-time All-Star was traded by Boston in 1956 for the right to draft Bill Russell and led the Hawks to the 1958 title.

briefs.headline: Bucks move home opener to afternoon to clear World Series Game 1
briefs.summary: The Oct. 23 game against Chicago tips at 4 p.m. ET instead of 8 p.m. ET so it does not run against the Brewers' Game 1 in Milwaukee that night, the team said Friday; the Bucks also host Cleveland Oct. 31, a possible Game 7 date.

briefs.headline: Hakkaku orders both yokozuna to take more practice bouts
briefs.summary: The Japan Sumo Association chairman, on his first visit to the autumn tour Friday in Kyoto, said neither Onosato nor Hoshoryu fully grasps the yokozuna (grand champion) rank; Hoshoryu, back from right-knee surgery, took 19 bouts and is aiming for the Kyushu basho (tournament), which opens Nov. 8 in Fukuoka, 22 days out.

briefs.headline: Hakuho named president of the International Sumo Federation
briefs.summary: The amateur governing body said Friday the 41-year-old former yokozuna (grand champion), who won a record 45 titles and left the JSA last year, takes the post; he said uniting the world through sumo is his mission.

prime.item: Day 3. Proclamation SF-1-2026, signed Oct. 2 at 3:10 p.m. by Division of Marine Fisheries interim director Michael S. Loeffler and re-opened this morning at 5:48 a.m. by its files.nc.gov address, made the hand harvest of oysters from public bottom in internal coastal fishing waters effective at sunrise Thursday, Oct. 15, and says the season closes March 31, 2027, under Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 03K .0201 unless closed sooner by proclamation. The recreational limit it sets is one bushel per person per day, not to exceed two bushels per vessel per day, seven days a week, from public bottom; it is unlawful to possess oysters under three inches shell length, to possess commercial and recreational limits aboard the same vessel, or to take them from the oyster sanctuaries designated in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117. The division's proclamations index, all six pages read at 5:49 a.m., lists SF-1-2026 as issued Oct. 2 and effective at sunrise Oct. 15; NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened at 5:48 a.m. and still dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, reads oysters as season closed, unlawful to possess, and the proclamation is the later document. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries.

NCDMF's recreational size and bag limits page, opened this morning at 5:48 a.m. and dated effective Sept. 2, 2026, lists red drum at an 18-inch minimum and 27-inch maximum total length and one per day, under federal red drum management; the division's flounder proclamation FF-27-2026, which the page links and which was re-read this morning with pdftotext, cites Marine Fisheries Commission rule 15A NCAC 3I .0124 requiring recreational anglers to report red drum, spotted seatrout, flounder, striped bass and weakfish harvest to the division. The proclamations index, all six pages read at 5:49 a.m., carries no 2026 recreational red drum proclamation. Topsail Sound is coastal water under the Division of Marine Fisheries, and the limits page says a Coastal Recreational Fishing License is required in coastal waters, a separate license from the inland one. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 16 days old, has red drum as the main inshore target around Topsail.

prime.dates: Open; 14- to 20-inch slot, one over 26 inches
prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists spotted seatrout, the speckled trout, at a 14- to 20-inch total-length slot with one fish over 26 inches allowed, three per day, no federal regulation. The division's proclamations index, read at 5:49 a.m., lists the harvest opening as FF-31-2026, issued June 25 and effective 12:01 a.m. July 1, 2026, and carries no later seatrout proclamation; the October proclamations on the index are the oyster opening, three commercial flounder orders and four gill net and stop net orders. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 16 days old, has the trout scattered, a few on early topwater, the guides waiting on cooler water.

prime.species: Spanish mackerel, king mackerel and bluefish
prime.item: NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists Spanish mackerel at 12 inches fork length and 15 per day, king mackerel at 24 inches fork length and three per day, and bluefish with no minimum size and five per day, all under federal management plans. The Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 16 days old, has Spanish and bluefish plentiful from the surf and piers and kings to 32 pounds at Jolly Roger Pier.

NCDMF's limits page, opened this morning, lists black drum at a 14-inch minimum and 25-inch maximum total length, 10 per day, sheepshead at 14 inches total length, five per day, neither under federal regulation, and spot with no minimum size and 50 per day under federal spot management. The reference calendar lists October as the peak of the spot run; the Oct. 1 Fisherman's Post report, 16 days old, has black drum of three to four pounds at the bridges and oyster reefs, spot in the evening bottom-fishing catch at Surf City Pier and sheepshead in the Seaview Pier bottom catch.

Surf at Ocean City Beach pier: high 12:13 AM at 3.4 ft, low 5:57 AM at 1.2 ft, high 12:48 PM at 4.5 ft, low 7:28 PM at 1.4 ft. waters.read: Fish the moving water either side of high at 1:21 AM and 1:55 PM in the sound.
waters.working: Seventh day past the new moon: the fetcher's file carries the moon as a waxing crescent, 36 percent lit and 6.0 days old, and the U.S. Naval Observatory's phase table, which answered at 5:48 a.m., puts the first quarter at 16:12 UT tomorrow, Sunday, Oct. 18, 12:12 p.m. ET, the full moon at 04:12 UT Oct. 26 and the last quarter at 20:28 UT Nov. 1, so today is the neap: the surf's midday high has come down from 5.3 feet Monday, 5.0 Tuesday, 4.6 Wednesday, 5.0 Thursday and 4.7 Friday to 4.5 today, and the sound's from 4.0 Friday to 3.9, the earlier figures cited from the week's editions. NWS Wilmington had no product for Coastal Pender (NCZ106) at 5:48 a.m., no rip current statement, no high surf advisory, no beach hazards statement, the sixth quiet beach morning in a row; a Beach Hazards Statement for a strong north-to-south longshore current, 6 a.m. to 8 p.m. today, covers Coastal New Hanover County (NCZ108), the next county down the coast, and stops there. What is on the water off the island is the Gale Warning, re-issued by the Wilmington office at 2:25 a.m. Saturday for the coastal waters from Surf City to Cape Fear out 20 nautical miles (AMZ250), the marine zone off the beach and the inlet: north winds 25 to 35 knots with gusts to 40 and seas 6 to 9 feet from noon today to 11 a.m. Monday, which the Service says will cause hazardous seas that could capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility. Friday's issue read 20 to 30 knots, seas 7 to 10 feet and an end at 6 a.m. Monday; the wind came up, the seas came down and the end moved five hours later. It is a marine product for the ocean out 20 miles, not a surf-zone or a sound product, and it takes effect about two hours before the sound's afternoon high. All four sound events fall inside Saturday this morning and none carries a spillover tag: the sound at Hampstead topped out at 3.1 feet at 1:21 a.m., is in the last 20 minutes of its ebb at press time, bottoming at a 1.0-foot low at 7:19 a.m., then fills 2.9 feet to a 3.9-foot high at 1:55 p.m. and drains 2.5 feet to a 1.4-foot low at 8:20 p.m.; the last two hours of that ebb, about 6:20 to 8:20 p.m., run into the evening. The surf at Ocean City Beach pier runs ahead and is the bigger water: high 12:13 a.m. at 3.4, low 5:57 a.m. at 1.2, high 12:48 p.m. at 4.5 and low 7:28 p.m. at 1.4, a 3.3- and 3.1-foot swing against Friday's 3.6 and 3.4. Today's lags from the two tables are 68 and 67 minutes on the highs and 82 and 52 minutes on the lows; the morning low again lags longest, the shallow sound draining slower than it fills, which stretches the drum window at the crew's spot past what a flat hour's offset would give. The water at Beaufort, 60 miles up the coast, read 77.0 degrees at 5:36 a.m., down 0.2 from Friday's 77.2. What is running is 16 days old, not a month: the Fisherman's Post Topsail and Sneads Ferry October report posted Thursday, Oct. 1, at 9 a.m. ET, and the feed carried it as its newest item at 5:48 this morning. East Coast Sports has slot red drum with over-slots mixed in off the surf and piers, Spanish and bluefish plentiful, kings showing more at the piers, trolled spoons working off the beach, and inshore red drum as the main target with no word on trout yet; Native Son has mullet everywhere and reds at the docks, creek mouths and grass lines, trout scattered, glass minnows thick off the beach and the kings still in 50 to 60 feet; Spring Tide has the reds schooled in the bays at 22 to 28 inches and better, topwater and artificials some days and cut bait others, trout quiet until the water cools, Spanish pushing inside the inlet on the high tide; Speckled Specialist has Carolina-rigged live mullet the best red drum bait, trout early on topwater and then live shrimp under slip corks in 15 to 20 feet, black drum of three to four pounds at the bridges and oyster reefs; Carolina Flats has big mullet moving into the ICW and the bigger reds on live finger mullet or artificials under popping corks, flounder as bycatch, false albacore due on the nearshore structure; Plan 9 has Spanish of 14 to 22 inches and false albacore just outside the inlet in 15 to 20 feet on small jigs; South End has the bigger Spanish in 45 to 50 feet over hard bottom under feeding birds and kings in the 8- to 12-mile range. The piers: Jolly Roger reports bait thick, multiple kings to 32 pounds, Spanish ramping up, and night bottom fishing producing red drum to 31 inches, Virginia mullet, pompano, bluefish, black drum and some flounder; Surf City Pier has good-sized Spanish on Gotcha plugs, slot and occasional over-slot reds, and evening bottom fishing with black drum, mullet, spot and croaker; Seaview Pier has the mullet migration starting, Spanish and bluefish on Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs, and a bottom mixed bag of flounder, sea mullet, spot, sheepshead, trout, black drum and the odd red. The reference calendar's October pattern, spot at peak, red drum, trout, bluefish, sea mullet and black drum, matches the report. On today's tides and this water, a tide problem before it is a lure problem: the sound is on the last of its morning ebb until 7:19 a.m., the red drum stage, but it ends 19 minutes after the paper posts, and the first full window of the day is the flood from 7:19 a.m. to 1:55 p.m., mud minnows and shrimp the forage on the oyster bars and grass edges as they cover, so a quarter-ounce gold spoon or a paddletail on a three-sixteenths-ounce head along the grass edges and across the oyster bars on the early flood, and a live shrimp on a slip cork at the oyster bars and the bridge pilings for the black drum and sheepshead as the bars go under. The 1:55 p.m. high puts 3.9 feet of water over the grass and up the dock pilings, a tenth less than Friday, which is where the reds go on a flooded high, so a topwater walked over the grass edges and down the dock lines on the last of the flood, about noon to 1:55 p.m., then a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig as the ebb starts; the Gale Warning's north wind is on the ocean side from noon, and the sound is outside its zone. The red drum window proper is the bottom of the afternoon ebb, roughly 6:20 to 8:20 p.m., 51 minutes later than Friday's and into the evening: finger mullet are the forage the file records and the report says the mullet are in, so a live finger mullet on a Carolina rig or a three-inch Gulp shrimp under a popping cork fan-cast a couple of feet off the channel edge where the creek mouths drain the grass, and a cut mullet chunk on the bottom at the same edge as the water gets low. On the evening flood after 8:20 p.m. the dock lights are the trout spot once the 36 percent crescent sets, though with Beaufort at 77.0 the cool-down the guides say the trout are waiting on has not come. Oysters are in their third day open under SF-1-2026 on the public bottom; the oyster bars the crew fishes over are the same structure, and the sanctuaries in rule 15A NCAC 03R .0117 are closed to harvest. The surf side is the morning only: Gotcha plugs and diamond jigs for the Spanish and bluefish on the flood to the 12:48 p.m. high, 4.5 feet of water at the pier, the pattern every pier in the report gives; from noon the Gale Warning's 25 to 35 knots of north wind and 6 to 9 feet of sea are on that water through Monday morning, and the evening cut-bait session for slot reds falls inside it. Slack at 7:19 a.m., 1:55 p.m. and 8:20 p.m. is dead water. Flounder are release only.
